name: Orangism
summary: Belgian Orangism was a 1830s-1850s current that rejected Belgian independence and wanted the southern provinces rejoined to the United Kingdom of the Netherlands under the House of Orange. It was directed by William I, drew many nobles, industrialists and officials of the old kingdom, and was strongest in Ghent and Liege. It was a loyalist, counter-revolutionary monarchism; its social and economic programme is largely undocumented.
scope: Belgian Orangism (the catalog entry linked to Orangism (Belgium)), c. 1830-1850, as a loyalist movement for restoring the 1815-1830 United Kingdom of the Netherlands under William I. It excludes the Dutch Orangism of the Republic and later Kingdom, Luxembourg Orangism, and Northern Irish Orangeism. Positions on matters the movement never addressed are inferred from its elite loyalist character and from the 1815 constitutional order it wanted back.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Nothing in the movement concerns health provision; an 1830s elite royalist movement would not expect state-run universal healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Minimum wages did not exist as policy; the industrialist and noble base would have opposed wage mandates.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: William I's state actively promoted trade and industry through state-backed institutions, so adherents were neither laissez-faire nor hostile to markets.

public-ownership.rationale: The Orangist elite included industrialists, and William's economic model used state-backed companies rather than public ownership of utilities.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The movement drew on nobles and industrialists, whose interests suggest resisting higher wealth taxes; no source addresses it.

unions-good.rationale: Unions were illegal or marginal in the 1830s and the movement's base was elite, so support is unlikely; inferred only.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property-owning nobles and industrialists dominated the movement, so strong property protection is inferred, not documented.

regulate-corporations.rationale: William I created and directed trading and industrial companies, so tight regulation was neither a theme nor clearly opposed.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare states did not exist; no position is documented and paternalist monarchism cuts both ways.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective worker ownership is alien to a movement of nobles and industrialists; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anachronistic; an authoritarian-leaning monarchy may accept state security measures but the movement was itself the target of state surveillance.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; conservative aristocratic leanings suggest opposition to drug legalization.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement ran an activist press and so valued press freedom against the new state, but no position on hate speech exists.

strong-leader.rationale: The Orangist cause centred on loyalty to a king who held near-autocratic powers, implying comfort with strong executive leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: Orangists wanted to restore an existing state under the House of Orange; abolishing the state is incompatible with that aim.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; Orangists organised armed brigades and coups, but no gun-law view is documented.

empower-police-military.rationale: Loyalists led Orangist brigades and wanted royal authority restored, so a strong security apparatus is inferred as congenial.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; conservative noble leanings suggest disapproval.

decide-locally.rationale: Orangists wanted the unitary kingdom restored, but they did contest provincial and municipal elections as a venue; overall centralised royal rule fits better.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy is not discussed in the sources; no inference is safe.

traditional-family.rationale: Noble Catholic and Protestant elites of the 1830s held conventional family norms; inferred only.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; an elite 19th-century conservative movement would have rejected it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Anachronistic; conventional religious and conservative norms of the era imply opposition.

more-religion-public.rationale: The movement was split between Protestant-leaning Dutch rule and Catholic nobles; William backed the Reformed Church while some Orangist nobles opposed secularism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a concern of the movement; no stance can be inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Orangists backed a union of Dutch and Belgian peoples, not defence of a separate Belgian national culture; the 'nation' in question is the united kingdom.

gradual-change.rationale: Orangists were counter-revolutionary loyalists who wanted restoration of the established dynasty and order, favouring established institutions.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anachronistic; the Great Powers' conferences decided Belgium's fate but Orangists did not argue about international organisations.

free-trade.rationale: The united kingdom's trade institutions and colonial commerce benefited industrial and port interests, and Orangism drew industrialists, so open trade within the union is plausible; not directly sourced.

nation-first.rationale: The movement subordinated Belgian independence to the Orange crown, but there is no stated view on national interest versus cooperation.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; conservative elite leanings imply opposition.

limit-growth.rationale: The kingdom prized industrial and commercial growth, so limiting growth runs against its priorities; inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: William I championed industrialisation and canals as routes to prosperity, suggesting optimism about technical progress; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Orangists treated the 1830 revolution as illegitimate and refused to take part in elections to its institutions, though they plotted coups to reverse it.

central-planning.rationale: The kingdom supported market-based trade through state-backed firms rather than planning; inferred.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cooperative or public ownership is foreign to the elite base; inferred.

land-value-tax.rationale: Landed nobles formed a core of the movement, who would oppose such a tax; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Noble families prizing inherited estates and titles would oppose heavy inheritance taxes.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Southern industry gained from state support, but the sources do not give the movement's tariff position.

state-directs-investment.rationale: William I's state founded and funded trade and industrial companies, indicating acceptance of directed investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The sources on the movement say nothing on spreading property among small owners versus corporations, so no position can be inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Anachronistic and wholly alien to the movement's elite base.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: William I founded state-sponsored financial institutions, so the model was institution-building, not abolition.

one-party-rule.rationale: Orangists contested provincial and local elections as a faction; the sources imply no party-state ideal.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The whole movement existed to restore the House of Orange, with William I directing it, so the legitimacy of the Orange monarch is its defining claim.

democracy-best.rationale: The 1815 constitution gave the crown near-autocratic powers and census suffrage, which the movement defended; the movement accepted no democratic ideal.

direct-votes.rationale: Direct legislation by referendum conflicts with the royal-authority model; William even counted abstentions as yes in 1815.

right-to-secede.rationale: Orangists denied the legitimacy of Belgium's secession from the united kingdom and sought to reverse it.

natural-rulers.rationale: Loyalist nobles valued hereditary rank and court privilege, implying belief in hereditary governing classes.

political-violence-never.rationale: At least three Orangist coups were attempted in the 1830s, so adherents did not reject political violence.

war-builds-character.rationale: No source links Orangism to a view that war improves national character; it was a restorationist political movement.

separate-church-state.rationale: William I officially separated church and state yet strongly backed the Reformed Church, and noble Orangists opposed secularising society.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Although religion mattered, the king's constitutional order was not scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A royalist state-restoring movement would reject privatised justice and defence.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The united kingdom joined Dutch-speaking, French-speaking, Protestant and Catholic peoples under one crown, an explicitly multi-ethnic state.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Elite conservative movement; class conflict as history's engine is alien.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hereditary privilege and aristocratic influence were part of the movement's ethos.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; Dutch colonial holdings are not discussed in sources.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The kingdom's colonial wealth was central to William's economy; reparations are anachronistic and unlikely.

civilizational-union.rationale: Orangists wanted two neighbouring peoples (Belgians and Dutch) reunited under one crown, a sympathetic case of union among kindred societies.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses whether self-interest is morally good; loyalty to the dynasty was the movement's stated driver.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Loyalty and duty to the sovereign and the dynasty are central to the Orangist stance; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The 1830s loyalist movement left no record on the intrinsic value of nature, so the answer is neutral.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The kingdom actively promoted industrialisation, which Orangist industrialists benefited from.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological advance was welcome but disrupting institutions was not.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred opposition from traditional monarchism.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Encryption did not exist in the period; there is no basis to infer a position.

restore-past-order.rationale: The movement's declared aim was to restore the pre-1830 United Kingdom of the Netherlands under the House of Orange.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The sources give no view on judging policy by results; the movement was defined by dynastic loyalty.

direct-action.rationale: Orangists used press, local elections and coups, but not mass direct action; adherents mainly relied on dynastic diplomacy.

means-match-ends.rationale: No source discusses whether methods should mirror goals; Orangists used press, local elections and coups.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Alien to an elite conservative movement.

production-for-use.rationale: Orangist industrialists produced for trade profit under the kingdom's commercial system.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Industrialist adherents would reject the claim.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Anachronistic; not a view the movement held.

taxation-theft.rationale: The movement wanted a taxing state restored under the crown; no libertarian view is documented.

harm-principle.rationale: Nothing in the record concerns the limits of state restriction on adults; no position inferable.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The movement did not argue about individual versus group rights in the sources reviewed.

conscription.rationale: The Orangists wanted the royal state restored, and the 1830s kingdom maintained conscription as a state-building tool; weakly inferred.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Not addressed; royalist loyalty is not exit-based.

state-as-business.rationale: William I ran the state through business-like trading companies, though no doctrine of citizens as customers appears.

positive-liberty.rationale: Freedom as material means was not a theme of this royalist movement as the sources describe it.

media-academia-power.rationale: The question concerns modern universities and media, which the 1830s movement never discussed.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The sources record no Orangist view on racial ability differences.

organic-representation.rationale: A noble and estate-minded elite would favour representation by rank and corporate body; inferred.

total-state.rationale: The movement was a monarchist counter-revolution, not totalitarian; no such programme.

national-rebirth.rationale: The aim was restoration of a prior order, not radical rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The aim was reuniting a lost territory, not expansion beyond it; no wider view documented.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Loyalist nobles bound to the king by gratitude and court favour; loyalty to the sovereign was central.

bound-labor.rationale: Not a position; serfdom was long gone.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: A postmodern epistemological claim with no counterpart in the movement's documented thought.

universal-morality.rationale: Conservative religious elites of the period generally held universal moral truths; inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Monarchist and conservative thought tends to see one common good guided by the crown; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The movement concerned Belgium and the Netherlands; Zionism is outside its documented concerns.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No diaspora or homeland-return issue appears in the sources on the Orangists.

revive-national-language.rationale: Dutchification under William promoted Dutch in Flanders, which some Flemish Orangists backed, but language revival as a general principle is not documented.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Industrialist adherents would resist workers' votes on firm governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: William I directed state education and founded universities; the Catholic church wanted autonomy instead, so adherents disagree little with state schooling.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The Dutch state was in financial difficulty, but no doctrine on deficits exists.

economic-freedom.rationale: The sources do not show Orangists tying political liberty to economic liberty.

rule-by-example.rationale: No source says Orangists favoured rule by moral example over law, so the answer stays neutral.

national-self-determination.rationale: Orangists rejected Belgium's claim to separate statehood and sought a reunited kingdom, denying that the Belgian nation should self-govern independently.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; the UN did not exist.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Opposition to a secular society is documented for the Orangist nobility, pointing away from rationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Modern welfare states did not exist then, and no Orangist view on immigrants' benefits is recorded.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Workfare is a modern policy that the movement never considered.

class-collaboration.rationale: Hierarchical paternalism of nobles and industrialists favours cooperation across classes; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Not a position of an elite monarchist movement tied to the Great Powers' settlement.

workers-nation.rationale: The movement was loyalist and elite, with no stance on how workers should organise.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Conventional noble norms of the era suggest support.

ban-interest.rationale: The kingdom built banks and credit institutions, so a ban on interest is contrary.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not part of the movement; contrary to its multi-peoples kingdom model.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist theory is alien to the movement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Oil and gas production was not a policy issue in the 1830s, so nothing can be inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration policy is not discussed in the sources on Orangism.

proportional-representation.rationale: The 1815 system gave equal seats to north and south despite population differences; no view on PR documented.

national-mission.rationale: No source ascribes to the movement a mission to spread its government form abroad.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Conventional view of the period implies disagreement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The movement was itself composed of the established elite and loyal court-connected nobility.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Anachronistic; not part of the movement.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The movement left no stance on prosecuting past abuses by state forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The kingdom's state actively promoted trade, education and canals.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not addressed; the multi-peoples kingdom model implies not.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Equality before the law was in the 1815 constitution's modest bill of rights, but noble privilege coexisted.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no connection to an 1830s monarchist movement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Orangism had no recorded view on how to classify settler states.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: No source records Orangist views on uniform civil law versus religion-based law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The kingdom guaranteed freedom of religion, so adherents would not restrict conversion.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: William I's schools were required to teach the Reformed faith, showing the regime favoured religion in state schooling.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Soviet-era doctrine without relevance to Orangism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Orangist legitimacy rested on dynastic right and the king's authority, not on popular consent, which the movement rejected when Belgians chose independence.

trade-surplus.rationale: The kingdom's merchantilist trading institutions aimed at export-driven commerce, but this is not documented as Orangist doctrine.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The movement plotted armed coups, and William I invaded in 1831.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The sources contain no Orangist doctrine about struggle as the engine of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party-ban doctrine is not discussed for the movement, which itself was hostile to Belgium's order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican concept of freedom as non-domination does not appear in Orangist sources.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1815 constitution had a bicameral legislature but concentrated executive power in the crown, so adherents were not committed to checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist party theory is wholly foreign to a loyalist, court-linked movement.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Paternalist noblesse may support charity, but no policy priority is documented.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing was a twentieth-century policy, so the movement had no stance.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Elite conservative base would favour restricting strikes; inferred.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The sources record no Orangist theory of the causes of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement defended a state spanning different languages and confessions as workable under one crown.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Royal authoritarian instincts imply accepting emergency powers; William used the rule of the crown vigorously in conflict.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: No Orangist position on food price caps is documented.

party-controls-media.rationale: The Orangists used an activist press themselves, so want press access rather than state control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not a party-state doctrine; the king commanded forces.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed in the sources on the movement.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: An elite movement would not hold this.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The movement was not organised as a disciplined party in the sources, so no inference.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Orangists favoured merging Belgium and the Netherlands into one kingdom, which is a form of political union, though not a supranational one.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The 1815 settlement the Orangists wanted restored left the king commanding the armed forces and appointing ministers answerable only to him.

church-by-bishops.rationale: William backed the Reformed Church, which has no bishops, while Catholic nobles in the movement accept bishops, so split.

clerical-rule.rationale: Neither the Reformed monarch nor the court elite wanted clerical government.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Wholly alien to a loyalist movement.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Orangist sources do not touch on censoring art for moral reasons.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not applicable to a hereditary monarchy.

recall-officials.rationale: Not compatible with the royal-appointed model.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The movement relied on Dutch support but no alliance doctrine appears.

people-in-arms.rationale: Orangist brigades were armed but the movement favoured the royal army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; agrarian nobles may sympathise.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reuniting Belgium with the Netherlands was the stated aim of Belgian Orangism, which treated the 1830 split as reversible.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-intellectual populism is not recorded as part of the movement.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The sources give no view on ranking cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Executions were normal in the 1830s, and a conservative monarchist base would accept them.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The evolution debate postdates the movement by decades.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: No source records Orangist views on how citizenship should pass.

minority-language-support.rationale: William's policy imposed Dutch in Flemish provinces while French stayed in Wallonia, showing state language policy was top-down, not minority support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general laws for minorities are not a documented Orangist question.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conformity to rank and order is more congenial than individualism; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: A financier-supporting regime would oppose debt cancellation.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not a view of the movement.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 1815 constitution was issued by the king and not written by an assembly, in the account of William I I read.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: No source ties Orangism to trading freedoms for development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Development aid is a twentieth-century concept outside the movement's world.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement by over a century.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Orangism's head of state is a hereditary monarch, so direct election is rejected.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Modern central-bank independence has no counterpart in the movement's debates.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: William I refused the first treaty and kept up the territorial dispute for years, a stance resisting concessions on land.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The sources do not show whether Orangists limited property to the common good.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A twentieth-century Marxist debate irrelevant to Orangism.

precautionary-principle.rationale: An environmental policy principle of the late twentieth century, unknown to the movement.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance mutual-defence clauses are not discussed in the Orangist record.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Orangists considered Belgium's separation illegitimate; applying to Belgium it is an extrapolation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: William I was state-dominant over churches in education, yet Catholic noble Orangists resented state encroachment.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: William I governed actively as head of government, so the monarch was not above politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: William I used force in 1830 and 1831 to try to retain the south, and Orangism sought to reverse secession.

region-keeps-system.rationale: No source records Orangist views on regions joining larger states with their own systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Orange monarchy was constitutional and Dutch Reformed in tradition, with no claim of divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax in the modern sense did not exist, so no position can be inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: The nature-versus-nurture question is not addressed in the sources.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The king was bound by a constitution, though it gave him near-autocratic powers.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration is far outside the movement's era.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The 1815 constitution mixed a hereditary crown, an appointed chamber and a census-elected chamber, but sources do not frame Orangists as advocating a mixed constitution.

leader-cult.rationale: Orangism had no documented leader-cult practice beyond loyalty to the king.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law presumptions are a modern question the movement never faced.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine with no bearing on Orangism.

refugee-return.rationale: The sources do not mention refugee return in the Orangist context.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Orangist reunification rested on the kingdom's former borders and shared Dutch-speaking Flemish ties; extrapolation.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The kingdom guaranteed freedom of religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress mandates for women were not a feature of the movement or of the Dutch-Belgian kingdom.

common-currency.rationale: Reunification with the Netherlands would have meant a shared currency, an implication not a stated aim.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Orangism sought to rejoin the Belgian and Dutch peoples under one crown, directly matching political unity across borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Language and school policy was set centrally by William, so cultural autonomy was not a principle.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources record no Orangist view on minorities seeking equal rights versus emigrating.

ban-cartels.rationale: No Orangist antitrust position is recorded in the sources.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank bailouts as a policy question did not exist then.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: No source records Orangist views on courts constraining majorities.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The kingdom lived on trade through Antwerp, Amsterdam and colonies, not autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding labour and environmental clauses in trade deals are modern, so no stance can be inferred.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not a view of the movement.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Orangists staged armed coups for counter-revolution, but the revolutionary-vanguard theory is irrelevant.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Orangist nobility gained privilege and influence from court favour and defended that order.

history-own-civilization.rationale: No source addresses how Orangists wanted history taught.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The sources do not report Orangist views on tutelage of less advanced societies.

patriotic-education.rationale: William's education system promoted Dutch language and the state-approved confession, indicating comfort with loyalty education.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a modern policy, so the movement had no view.

public-money-creation.rationale: Modern monetary reform proposals were beyond the movement's concerns.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Industrialist base would hold this; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The movement aimed at renewing union, not influence abroad.

delink-world-market.rationale: The kingdom thrived on world trade.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist theory unrelated to Orangism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: No Orangist position on private discrimination is recorded.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1815 constitution had a limited unentrenched bill of rights, so adherents were not committed to entrenchment.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Orangists accepted the Treaty of London's finality only reluctantly, but a general rule against colonial treaties is unrelated.

elective-rulers.rationale: Orangists wanted the hereditary House of Orange to rule, not an elected ruler.

minority-veto.rationale: The monarchist model implies binding decisions by the crown.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Orangists stressed loyalty to the king, and ministerial responsibility was opposed by William I as a conservative.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The movement defended the 1815 order in which the crown, not parliament, held decisive authority.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not discussed in the sources on Orangism.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The movement's noble leadership is associated with paternalist duty, though not directly documented.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Orangists were politically active through the press, elections and coups.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt School cultural critique is unrelated to the movement.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony theory has no connection to the movement.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The kingdom profited from colonial wealth, so adherents would not see extraction as a problem.

native-born-offices.rationale: Not addressed; the united kingdom drew officials from both north and south.

party-own-road.rationale: A communist-movement question with no counterpart in Orangism.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Development-aid debates are outside the movement's era.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The movement's aim was to regain Belgium, which the Netherlands had lost in 1830.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Colonial indigenous politics is not discussed in the Orangist sources.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Fascism did not exist in the 1830s.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Totalitarianism as a category postdates the movement.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: An American historical dispute unrelated to Orangism.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Conservative respect for inherited symbols is inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The question concerns modern gender debates absent from the movement.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: A modern debate that the movement did not address.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: No source records a view that political institutions should vary by civilisation.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Orangist brigades and officers were counter-revolutionary; the military as guardian of order fits, though not documented.

office-by-exam.rationale: Not addressed; court favour was a basis of noble advancement.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Cross-border takeovers of strategic firms were not an issue in the period.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The States General had limited power under the 1815 constitution; adherents' view on budget approval is not documented.

single-official-language.rationale: William's Dutchification made Dutch the sole language in some provinces but French remained in Wallonia, and Flemish and Walloon Orangists differed.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The sources do not discuss restrictions on foreign landowners.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A modern legal doctrine absent from the movement.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Mass consumerism was not yet a social issue for the movement to judge.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The sources do not record Orangist views on supporting insurgents abroad, apart from the Dutch king's own war.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Bloc intervention doctrines are twentieth-century concepts.

corporate-influence.rationale: Industrialist adherents would not see corporate influence as a problem.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not addressed; Orangists themselves were funded by Dutch money.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: No source records Orangist family-size policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchases are not discussed in the sources.

democratic-peace.rationale: The democratic-peace theory belongs to later political science.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Loyalist conservatives held a strong duty of obedience to lawful authority.

non-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; the Great Powers did intervene in 1830-39.

industrial-unions.rationale: Industrial unions were not a live question for an 1830s elite movement.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The sources contain no conspiracy claim about a minority from the Orangists.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Freedom of information laws are modern, so no stance exists.

local-production.rationale: The kingdom's economy was based on trade, not localism.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement had a hierarchical, court-linked structure.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The sources do not report Orangist views on the primacy of national law.

religious-nation.rationale: The united kingdom spanned Reformed and Catholic subjects, so a single religion did not define the nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tribute-based deference is not part of the movement's thought.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The unitary kingdom pooled resources north and south; adherents lacked a regionalist line.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communism as a political force post-dates the movement.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models were not discussed by Orangists.

religion-illusion.rationale: Opposition to secular society is documented for Orangist nobles.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The kingdom promoted industrialisation, which Orangist industrialists favoured; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language purism is not documented in the Orangist sources.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; Orangists contested the Treaty of London for years.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Not a part of the movement.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Third-way doctrines belong to the twentieth century.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Orangists framed Belgium as legitimately belonging under the House of Orange by prior union; extrapolated.

suppress-opposition.rationale: William I's rule was near-autocratic, but his opponents in 1830s Belgium were the ones in power, and Orangists claimed press freedom.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: William I's regime favoured the Reformed Church, but the kingdom guaranteed freedom of religion.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Colonial profits mostly went to Dutch directors, which was a documented grievance and characteristic of the system the movement wanted back.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious doctrine of Islam with no bearing on the movement.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A doctrine of Islamist movements with no bearing on the Orangists, who defended a legitimate monarch.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The crown-centred constitution offered limited participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Intersectionality is a modern theory the movement never considered, and its worldview was hierarchical.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The left-right debate in this form is modern, so the movement had no view.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The movement's sources do not touch on Islam or Muslim immigration.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Orange monarchism appealed to dynastic right, and Catholic nobles may have invoked God, but no source documents divine authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: No source records Orangist views on religious dress in public institutions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Nondisclosure agreements are modern legal tools unknown to the movement.

social-market-economy.rationale: The social market economy is a postwar German concept with no Orangist counterpart.

rich-first.rationale: Development sequencing was not debated by the movement.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Not addressed; Belgium was neutralised by treaty in 1839.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Orangist cause was dynastic restoration of the House of Orange, with succession by descent.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The kingdom's banking was commercial, not mutual.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: IMF-style lender conditions did not exist then.

property-franchise.rationale: The 1815 constitution used census suffrage, which the Orangists wanted restored.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is modern, and a conservative loyalist movement would disagree with it.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept unrelated to Orangism, with no record of the movement discussing it.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The movement ran an activist press and wanted its freedom.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The constitutional order the movement defended gave laws and codes through the State General, a basic rule-of-law outlook; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: The internet did not exist in the movement's era.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data practices are modern, so no position can be drawn.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The kingdom's mixed Catholic and Protestant population makes restriction unlikely, yet no documented view.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Sortition-based assemblies are modern, and the movement's elite royalism suggests disagreement.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The sources do not show Orangists calling for reinterpretation of religious doctrine.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The Orangist nobility opposed secularisation of society.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Alien to a royalist order movement.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The united kingdom allocated equal seats to north and south to balance two communities, which fits a power-sharing logic.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Paternalist noble leanings imply this; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Not compatible with hereditary rule or court-linked elites.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is a modern idea that conflicts with the movement's royalist model.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Extinction risk is a modern concern foreign to the movement.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Conventional norms of the era imply patriarchal marriage.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: No source records Orangist views on noncitizen voting.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Uniformed youth movements are twentieth-century phenomena unrelated to Orangism.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear weapons did not exist in the era.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Permanent foreign basing of the modern kind did not exist in the movement's era.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Genocide recognition is a modern concept absent from the movement's era.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Landowning and industrial adherents would defend ownership income.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The sources record no Orangist theory of national continuity from ancient times.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: A recent academic theory conflicting with the traditional outlook of the movement's elite base.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A recent feminist-theory position unrelated to Orangism and at odds with its conservatism.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The sources show no Orangist cult of martyrs for the nation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The sources do not frame Orangism as a spiritual struggle between good and evil.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The diaspora-homeland relationship is not an Orangist theme.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement was state-first, aiming at a political restoration.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A feminist theology position foreign to the movement and at odds with its traditional religious elites.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Orangism is not recorded as asking for economic dominance by one ethnic group.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Orangism reunited Dutch-speaking Flanders with the Netherlands; the Greater Netherlands movement it inspired shares this aim, though not all of it was monarchist.

independent-unions.rationale: Unions were not a live Orangist issue, so no position can be inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: A socialist definitional claim foreign to a royalist movement.

local-essentials-public.rationale: No source records Orangist views on public ownership of local services.

second-chamber.rationale: The 1815 constitution had a bicameral States General with an appointed First Chamber and elected Second Chamber, which the movement sought to restore.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal ownership of production belongs to anarchist and socialist thought, not to royalist Orangism.

family-wage.rationale: The sources say nothing on wage-setting for family support.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation of that kind did not exist in the movement's time.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research funding is far outside the movement's era.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Digital payments did not exist then.

online-anonymity.rationale: The internet is outside the movement's era.

person-over-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss whether the state serves the person; the movement defended a monarchical state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Religious elites of the time held this; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: A unitary kingdom gives regions no entrenched powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Genetic engineering is far outside the movement's era.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban density and environment were not debated by Orangists.

racial-pride.rationale: The sources do not record Orangist views on racial pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: William I invaded in 1831 to retain the south, so war was not only defensive.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The united kingdom crossed linguistic lines and its supporters rejected linguistic nationalism as a basis of statehood.

communal-electorates.rationale: No source records Orangist views on religion-based electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The sources show no Orangist narrative of foreign plots to partition the country, though the movement itself sought to reunite it.

free-public-college.rationale: William founded universities at Leuven, Ghent and Liège in 1817, suggesting state-supported higher education, but tuition policy is not documented.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Pollution taxation is a late-twentieth-century idea outside the movement's era.

future-generations.rationale: Intergenerational environmental duty is a modern theme absent from the sources.

arms-reduction.rationale: The sources record no Orangist stance on arms reduction.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Dynastic diplomacy was conducted privately by the crown.

capital-controls.rationale: The trading kingdom's finance depended on free capital movement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: A royalist state-restoring movement would favour state monopoly over arms, though Orangists themselves formed armed brigades.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits for low-paid workers are modern welfare design absent from the era.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Statutory debt limits are modern, so no position can be inferred.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Global economic restructuring demands are a twentieth-century theme.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Orangists sought to restore the state, not smash it.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Natural-capital accounting is modern and unknown to the movement.

sacred-nation.rationale: The sources describe a dynastic loyalty, not a sacralised nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student loans did not exist in the period.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Southern Belgian grievances against Dutch dominance of colonial profits shaped the revolution that Orangists opposed.

public-service-media.rationale: Public broadcasting did not exist in the movement's time.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Confessional loyalties among nobles imply disagreement.

farm-price-support.rationale: The sources do not record Orangist views on crop price guarantees.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear weapons postdate the movement by over a century.

ban-fgm.rationale: The sources record no Orangist view on female genital cutting.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; Orangist families were landed.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Dutch language policy under William treated Flemish as Dutch,.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Environmental tort liability is a modern doctrine outside the movement's era.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary chiefs do not feature in Belgian or Dutch Orangist politics.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Environmental priority over liberty is a modern debate; the movement had no stance and its elite base would not likely prioritise it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: The sources record no Orangist view on judicial discretion in sentencing.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: No source states Orangist views on language requirements for immigrants.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Private noble and bourgeois landownership underlay the movement's base, so community-held land is rejected; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis for a position.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: As a loyalist movement of nobles and industrialists, it would be hostile to compulsory unions, but the sources do not discuss it and the issue is anachronistic; inferred.

voter-id.rationale: The movement favoured a restricted, property-based order, so tight voting controls would suit it; inferred, as the sources do not discuss identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1815 order protected the equal standing of the churches under a Protestant king, though noble Orangists also opposed a secular society; inferred.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: William I's near-autocratic constitution and the loyalist counter-revolution put the monarch before elected rulers; inferred that adherents would not define democracy by elections alone.

premarital-sex.rationale: Orangist nobles opposed secular society and held conservative religious morals; inferred, not stated in the sources.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: A loyalist order-minded movement would accept state control for order; inferred, as the sources predate the technology.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The movement of nobles, officials and industrialists favoured the existing social order and William I's economic policy rather than cash welfare; inferred, anachronistic.

women-suffrage.rationale: The 1815 constitutional order the movement wanted back gave political rights to men of property only; inferred that women's suffrage would not be supported.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The movement was socially conservative and tied to church and crown, so would reject this view; inferred, anachronistic.

race-social-construct.rationale: Racial categories were not a question in the movement's 1830s politics, and the sources do not address it; indifferent.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: State bodies for gender equality are far outside the 1830s loyalist order; inferred, anachronistic.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the property-owning elite the movement drew from would not be hostile, but no position is documented.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic: international criminal courts did not exist in the 1830s, so no position can be inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; the 1815 kingdom was religiously mixed and adherents are not documented either way.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the movement's subject; no position can be inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Inferred: a loyalist, counter-revolutionary monarchism of nobles and industrialists would oppose nationalised property and planning.

indirect-election.rationale: Inferred: the 1815 constitutional order it wanted restored chose the lower house through provincial bodies rather than by direct vote; the sources opened do not detail it.

national-church-status.rationale: Inferred: a Protestant dynasty ruled a largely Catholic south, so adherents would have been split on a privileged national church.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: the movement sought a unitary kingdom under William I, not regional autonomy for a minority.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Inferred: Orangists rejected the result of the 1830 revolution and the 1839 settlement rather than accepting a local vote on the territory's allegiance.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic: the 1830 split was not a colonial independence; no position can be inferred.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred: its leadership was drawn from nobles and industrialists with an elite lifestyle, so asceticism is not part of it.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred: an elite, centralising loyalism would not restrict settlement for an indigenous majority; the sources do not address it.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred: 1830s conscription applied to men only, and a movement of old-order loyalists would not have sought equal female service.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The movement's concern was dynastic and constitutional, not a homeland bond; inferred.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The 1815 constitutional order it wanted back had legal process; inferred.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic for the 1830s; no position can be inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The movement sought to rejoin the south to the Netherlands, not diaspora policy; anachronistic.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: An elite loyalist movement would not hold that appropriating resources creates compensation duties; inferred.

self-ownership.rationale: Its industrialists and nobles favoured property and personal freedoms under the 1815 order; inferred.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; anachronistic.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: An elite royalist movement is inferred to favour limited, targeted relief.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Nobles and officials of a constitutional monarchy are inferred to value established institutions; but William I's prerogative makes this uncertain.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Royal patronage of industry under William I favoured connected firms; inferred.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Catholic and Protestant tensions existed under William I; adherents are inferred to be split.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Anachronistic for the 1830s; no position can be inferred.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: A conservative noble movement is inferred to resist expanding women's legal independence.

national-resource-control.rationale: A loyalist movement for the Netherlands' state is inferred to favour domestic control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The movement drew nobles, industrialists and officials of the old kingdom, so it would defend inherited property and market outcomes; inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Anachronistic for an 1830s movement; its merchant and industrial supporters favoured open trade, so they would not welcome a tax on it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement never addressed racial groups.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: A loyalist, legitimist movement stood for order and the lawful king; it contested the legitimacy of Belgian institutions, so adherents may be split, but a general right to disobey unjust law is unlikely.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Anachronistic; an elite royalist movement of the 1830s had no stance on automation and would likely value employment and the existing order.

multipolar-world.rationale: The 1815 order it wanted back rested on the post-Napoleonic balance among powers, so it would favour several centres of power; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Anachronistic; the nobles and industrialists behind it had no reason to credit labour alone with value, but the sources do not discuss it.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: An elite loyalist movement tied to the dynasty rather than to working people; its loyalty was to the House of Orange, not a politics for workers.

material-over-identity.rationale: Anachronistic; there was no left in the modern sense and the sources are silent on this.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Anachronistic; a monarchist movement of property owners would reject communist party rule.

missingStatements.text: A country that has split from a neighbour should be reunited with it under a shared ruling dynasty.
missingStatements.rationale: Rejoining Belgium to the Netherlands under the House of Orange was the movement's defining aim.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to the Belgian-Dutch split; not a question other ideologies take a side on (reunify-divided-nation covers the general idea).

missingStatements.text: Citizens may rightly refuse to take part in national elections of a state they regard as illegitimate.
missingStatements.rationale: Orangists boycotted national parliamentary elections but contested provincial and municipal ones.
missingStatements.declined: Idiosyncratic tactic of one movement; not a defining position across ideologies.

notes: Sources document the movement's constitutional aims and social base but say little about its economic or social programme, so nearly all answers beyond monarchy, reunion and counter-revolution are low-confidence inferences.
